messages:
Abby: Escalation — customer tried to issue a refund via our public API but got a 400 and we created an internal note instead of processing the refund. Case INC-3427, user is blocked. Payload + logs below.

InfraBot: [router] autorouter-v2 picked tool=post_internal_note request_id=req_8a3f91cb confidence=0.32 fallback=manual_note_created

Kevin: Can you paste the original request body and the error response?

Abby: Sure — reproducer curl and body:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/support/action \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "customer_id": 987654,
    "action": "refund",
    "amount": "10.00",
    "currency": "USD",
    "reason": "Duplicate charge, please refund",
    "source": "support_ui"
  }'
```
Response: HTTP 400
```
{
  "error": "schema_validation",
  "details": "amount must be integer cents",
  "request_id": "req_8a3f91cb"
}
```
Router fallback log shows it then created an internal note instead of issuing refund:
```
[INFO] -> executed tool=post_internal_note note_id=note_5532 for request_id=req_8a3f91cb
```

Rebecca: Hypothesis: the refund tool signature expects amount_cents:int. The request used amount as a decimal string "10.00" so schema match failed. The autorouter then fell back to fuzzy NLP matching and picked post_internal_note because of the word "note"/"reason" text. We should not let free-text fields steer tool choice when a billing intent is present.

Kevin: Quick repro I ran locally: if amount is integer (1000) autorouter picks issue_refund. If string "10.00" it picks post_internal_note. Repro steps: 1) POST above with "amount":1000 -> tool=issue_refund -> 200. 2) change to "10.00" -> tool=post_internal_note -> 400 + note.

Josh: From eng-runtime: thanks for the details — this is a routing + schema normalization gap. Plan (short):
- Add a small normalization layer in the support ingress that attempts to coerce common amount formats ("10.00", "10", "10 USD") -> amount_cents:int before routermatch.
- Penalize post_internal_note in the routing model for requests that contain explicit billing intents (action=refund, keywords: refund/charge/duplicate).
- Add an alert on fallback_to_note rate for billing endpoints.
I'll open a PR for the normalization and the model tweak; canary the change in support region.

Abby: Customer is on hold and needs this today. Can we hotfix normalization in the support ingress (middleware) as a patch while model retraining goes through?

Josh: Yes — will push a config-only change that enables amount parsing heuristics. Rolling a canary now. :rocket:

InfraBot: Deploy started: deploy_id=deploy_2026-03-17-01 component=support-ingress canary_instances=2

Kevin: Once canary is up, we'll need a log showing autorouter picking issue_refund + HTTP 200. Also add automated test for the three formats: integer cents, decimal string, currency-suffixed string.

Rebecca: I'll add the unit + e2e tests and update the routing playbook. Also adding a short note in docs about acceptable amount formats.

Abby: Thanks — please @Josh or me when canary shows green. I'll update INC-3427 and notify the customer. :thumbsup:

Josh: Canary passed on instance=1, instance=2. New logs: 
```
[router] request_id=req_8a3f91cb tool_match=issue_refund confidence=0.87 matched_signature=refund_v3 normalized_amount_cents=1000
[api] request_id=req_8a3f91cb response=200 refund_id=rf_7721
```
InfraBot: Deploy finished: deploy_id=deploy_2026-03-17-01 status=success

Kevin: Great — I'll close the loop after unit tests land. Also proposing a small heuristic: if action=="refund" prefer numeric coercion before doing fuzzy text match.

Abby: Closing the customer loop. Marking INC-3427 as resolved after confirmation. Thanks team. :pray:
